questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. **

I do not see __some reasons why__ my application should be rejected.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2.**

__
 
• 'Some', 'any', and 'many' are determiners.__
 
• **'Some'** is used in __positive sentences.__
 
• **'Any'** is used in a __negative sentence__ that has 'not'.

Thus, **'some'** must be replaced with **'any'.**

The correct sentence will be: *I do not see __any reason why__ my application should be rejected.*

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error' **

As a child, she was afraid from darkness.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4.**

**'from darkness'** is erroneous. It must be replaced with **'of darkness'.**

**Darkness** is a state of being dark, where there is no little or no light.

The sentence talks about the little child being afraid in a situation where it is dark.

Thus the correct sentence will be: *As a child, she was afraid of darkness.*

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

The Principal has said, "Mr. Surinder will coach the football team."

options.text: The Principal has said if Mr. Surinder would coach the football team.
The Principal has said that Mr. Surinder will coach the football team.
The Principal said that Mr. Surinder would coach the football team.
The Principal has asked that will Mr. Surinder coach the football team.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2.**

The given sentence is an **assertive sentence in Direct speech**. It will be converted in **Indirect speech.**

When we convert from direct speech to indirect speech, the following changes take place:

 
• **The tense of the Reported Verb does not change.**
 
• *The **verb in the reported speech** **does not undergo any change **if the **reporting verb is in the present or future tense. **Here, the reporting verb is in the** present perfect tense** and hence the** verb in the reported speech 'will coach' will remain as it is. ***
 
• Determiner **'that' is added** and inverted commas are omitted.

Following the changes, the indirect speech will be: *The Principal has said that Mr. Surinder will coach the football team.*

When we convert a sentence from direct to indirect speech, we make the following changes:

 
• **Quotation marks** are **omitted** and the sentence** ends with a full stop**. 
 
• The **tense** of the **verb**, in the reported speech involving any **order, request and instruction** does** not undergo** any **change **during the conversion from direct to indirect mode. This is also true if the statement is a** universal truth.** 
 
• If the** reporting verb** is in the **present tense**, it does **not undergo** any **change**.
 
• We add the word** 'to' **before the verb if the verb is in the **bare infinitive**.
 
• When the reporting or **principal verb** is in the **present tense**, all present tenses of the direct are **changed** into the corresponding** past tenses.**
 
• Words expressing **nearness in time or place** are generally converted into words expressing** distance**.

 For eg.** now** becomes **then**,** today** becomes **that day**, **yesterday** becomes **the previous day**, **this** becomes** that,** etc.
 
• In reporting **commands and requests**, the** verb expressing command or request **is **added** and the** imperative **is changed into the** infinitive.** 
 
• In reporting** questions** the** verbs like asked inquired** are **added** 
 
• In reporting** exclamations and wishes**, the** verbs expressing exclamation or wish** are **added**. 
 
• When we convert a sentence from the direct to the indirect mode(especially for a sentence** ending** with a** mark of interrogation**), we** reverse** the **subject-verb placement.** In **direct** sentences, we have the **verb before the subject**; while in** indirect,** the **verb follows the subject.**

Thus other options are incorrect as they do not follow the rules of conversion.

questions.solution:

**Fragrant** is the antonym of **foul.**

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

She is teaching French to children.

options.text: Children were taught French by her.
Children are being taught French by her.
Children are taught French by her.
Children have been taught French by her.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2.**

The given sentence is an assertive sentence in the **active voice**. It's structure is **Subject + helping verb + present continuous tense + Direct object + Indirect object.**

She + is + teaching + French + to + children.

When we convert the sentence in **Passive Voice**, its structure is: Indirect Object + is / am / are + being + V2 + Direct Object + by + Subject.

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error' **

Plenty of information were given to me at the tourist ofﬁce.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1.**

The error is in the phrase **'were given to me'.**

__As per the Subject-Verb agreement, 'Plenty of' is followed by an uncountable noun (information). It takes a singular verb.__

Thus, **'were'** must be replaced with **'was'.**

The correct sentence will be: *Plenty of information was given to me at the tourist ofﬁce.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. **

Having __being warn__ before, he did not repeat the mistake.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The sentence is in the **Present Perfect Continuous tense**.

 
 
• Its structure is '**have/has + been + V1 + ing' **in the active voice.
 
• Its structure is** have/has + been + being + past participle** in the passive voice.
 
 
 
• The given sentence is in the passive voice, and the use of tense is incorrect.
 
• **'being warned'** must be replaced with **'been warned'**.

 

Thus the correct sentence will be: *Having **been warned **before, he did not repeat the mistake.*
